main_body: Hospital bed seen from the front: a pillow, white sheet and blue blanket in a gray frame, with a headboard of vertical bars at the top. It is a tall, narrow object about 36 rows high.
top_band: none. The column starts with a light gray headboard band (rows 11-13) and dark vertical bars (rows 14-19). Below them are a pillow, sheet and blanket drawn face-on. No horizontal surface is seen from above.
evidence: Reading one column down the middle: the headboard rim (rows 11-13), the bars (14-19), a dark line (20-21), then a gray band (22-23). After that come the pillow and sheet (24-32) and the blue blanket (33-37) as one vertical stack. The bed looks as if it were standing upright and seen from the front. There is no foreshortened mattress top and no front edge line with an eave shadow. The sheet and blanket are vertical faces, not a surface seen from above. This is a front elevation, and the thin light band at the top is only a rim.

style.evidence: The candidate has about 4 lightness steps in its grays and whites, against 5-6 in the reference. The outline is a dark neutral gray-blue that leans toward near-black along the edges. The pillow and sheet are large flat white and gray areas with no grain or texture dots. Many tiles have only 2-4 colours, well below the information-rich reference tiles (the stall and the well).
